focus.label: Lightning-induced eye injury
focus.why: Direct lightning strike (node-2) plus delayed posterior subcapsular cataract and macular thickening (node-4) are classic electrical ocular injury; initial normal exam (node-3) does not exclude delayed findings.

payload.query: Need the patient's detailed ophthalmology consultation records, including slit-lamp examination for posterior subcapsular cataract and OCT for macular thickening, plus serial visual acuity assessments to confirm the delayed onset and rule out alternative causes.

payload.analysis: OCT shows delayed right macular thickening and outer retinal disruption at two weeks, partial restoration at four months, fitting lightning injury. payload.report: Vision loss began four days after a forehead lightning strike. Initial exam was normal, but follow-up OCT showed delayed macular thickening and outer retinal disruption at two weeks, partially restored at four months, plus cataract. These temporally linked findings cannot be explained by functional vision loss or pre-existing disease; the delayed pattern fits lightning injury. Missing slit-lamp/ERG and unverified cataract limit certainty, but lightning-induced eye injury is most probable.
